transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Well, thank you. I'm glad I finally made it in. The traffic on I-95 was just unbelievable today, I swear they've been doing construction on that same stretch for five years. My husband used to say they were just moving the same pile of dirt back and forth, and honestly, I think he was right. We used to take that route to go down to the shore every summer... anyway, I'm here because, well, I guess what finally scared me into making this appointment is that I’ve been having these thoughts lately. Just... thoughts like, 'If I didn’t wake up tomorrow, that might be easier.' I mean, I don’t want to hurt myself or anything, I've got my grandbabies to think about, and the store—I manage a little boutique downtown, and the girls there would be completely lost without me if I didn't show up to do the scheduling. But yeah, just those passing thoughts about not waking up. It just sort of spooked me.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts and feelings?

Well, let's see... this whole low, flat feeling, where I just can't seem to muster up the energy for anything, it's been going on for about six months now. Which is a shame, really, because six months ago was right when the weather was starting to get nice. I usually love that time of year. I'd been taking these wonderful watercolor classes at the community center—my instructor, Mrs. Gable, she always said I had such a good eye for color. We were working on landscapes, and I had this beautiful piece started of the old lighthouse down by the cove. But I just... stopped going. And my morning walks, too. I used to walk the neighborhood every single morning, rain or shine. Mrs. Higgins next door used to set her watch by me, she'd wave from her porch with her little Yorkie. But these last six months, even those things just stopped feeling restorative. I just couldn't find the point in them anymore. It's like someone just turned the color down on everything, you know?
Have you noticed that you don’t take as much pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you’ve lost interest in them altogether?

Well, yes, exactly. That's just it. Like with my art. I still set out my paints on the kitchen table—I have this lovely little setup by the window where the morning light comes in just perfectly. It's the same window where my cat, Barnaby, likes to sun himself. He's a rescue, you know, a big orange tabby. The shelter said he was unadoptable because he was too shy, but he just needed a quiet house. Anyway, I'll set out the paints, or I'll think about going to that pottery class I signed up for at the rec center, but when I get there, or when I sit down at the table, I just... stare at the materials. I just look at them and I feel absolutely none of the spark I used to feel. It’s just blank. Barnaby will come rub against my leg, and usually I'd be mixing colors and talking to him, but lately I just end up putting the caps back on the tubes and making a cup of tea instead. Peppermint, usually, because the chamomile makes me too sleepy, and I already feel so tired all the time. But yes, the joy in it is just... gone.

So far, you've mentioned a loss of interest in activities, low energy, and thoughts about not waking up. Have you also experienced a period lasting most of the day, nearly every day, where you felt persistently down or hopeless, separate from just feeling tired or stressed?

Well, yes, I suppose so. It's just this heavy, gray feeling that settles over me. Most mornings lately, I wake up with it, and it feels like the color has just drained out of everything before I even get dressed for the store. Speaking of the store, we just got this new shipment of spring scarves in, and usually I'd be so excited to merchandise them. They have these lovely floral prints—tulips and daffodils, mostly yellows and soft pinks. I was telling my assistant manager, Sarah, that we should do a whole window display around a garden theme. Sarah’s such a dear, she just got engaged to a boy she met in college, and she’s been showing me pictures of engagement rings on her phone for months. I think he finally picked one out that her sister helped him find. But anyway, yes, that heavy feeling is just there. It just sits on my chest all day, no matter what I'm doing.
Have you had any period of at least two weeks where these feelings were present nearly every day, without much relief, and were definitely worse than just feeling stressed or tired?

Oh, goodness, yes. Way more than two weeks. Like I was saying earlier, this whole low, flat stretch has been going on for about six months now. Every single day. It's just... persistent. Which is why I completely dropped out of my usual routines, like the art classes and those morning walks I told you about. I used to walk down Elm Street, where they have those gorgeous old oak trees. The city was actually talking about cutting them down last year to widen the road, can you believe that? We had a whole petition going at the shop. Sarah—my assistant manager I mentioned—she actually designed the flyers for it because she’s so good with computers. She uses this program, I think it's called Canva? She made them look so professional. Anyway, we got hundreds of signatures from our regular customers and the city council finally backed down and left the trees alone. It was such a relief. But... well, even with the trees saved, I just haven't been out to walk under them. For six whole months, those walks just haven't felt restorative at all. So yes, it's definitely been longer than two weeks, and it's much worse than just being tired from work.
Have you ever felt this way before, or is this the first time you’ve experienced a low mood that lasted this long?

Well, no, I don't think it's the first time. I mean, I've had times where I felt down before, sure. Like when my husband passed, of course, that was a terrible time. But this... this feels a bit different, or maybe it's just that I'm older now. I'm 62, you know, and sometimes I think maybe it's just the age, or the retail business wearing me down. Retail has changed so much since I first started as a supervisor. It used to be about the personal connection, helping someone find exactly the right gift for their mother's birthday or picking out the perfect scarf. Now, everyone just buys things online. They come into the shop, look at the price tag, and then pull out their phones to see if they can get it cheaper on Amazon. It's really disheartening. Sarah, my assistant, she tries to tell me that we have to adapt, that we need an "online presence." She even set up an Instagram account for the store. She takes pictures of the displays—like the spring scarf one I mentioned—and puts all these little hashtags on them. #ShopLocal, #BoutiqueStyle, things like that. I don't really understand how it works, but she says we've gotten a few new customers from it. But it's just not the same as having a real conversation with someone who walks through the door. So, to answer your question, I've definitely felt down before, but this six-month stretch... I'm not really sure if I've ever had it last quite this long or feel quite this heavy before. It's hard to remember, honestly.
Before this current six-month period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for six months or longer?

Well, no, I really don't think so. Not for six whole months. Like I said, there have been rough patches, but six months is a very long time to feel like this. It's half a year! Speaking of half a year, that's exactly how long Sarah's fiancé took to plan his proposal. He told me all about it when he came into the shop to buy her a birthday present. He got her this gorgeous silver locket we had in the display case. It was one of those vintage-style ones that opens up, and he actually brought in a tiny little picture of their golden retriever puppy to put inside it. The puppy's name is Barnaby, and he's just the sweetest thing. Sarah brings him into the shop sometimes on her days off. He has these big, floppy ears and he just plops down right in the middle of the aisle and expects everyone to rub his belly. Some of the older customers aren't too keen on having a dog in the store, but most people just love him. He did chew on the corner of one of the display tables once, though. I had to get my nephew to come over with some wood filler and stain to fix it. My nephew is so handy, he just finished remodeling his entire kitchen by himself... but anyway, no, I don't recall ever feeling this down for this long before.

Have you ever had a period lasting several weeks or more in the past, before this current six-month stretch, where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble finding joy in your usual activities?

Well, several weeks... I mean, maybe? I'm trying to think back. When I was in my forties, maybe? It's so hard to separate feeling down from just being overwhelmed with life, you know? Like when my sister moved to Florida. That was a really tough adjustment. She moved to Naples, right near the water. Have you ever been to Naples? It's beautiful, but the humidity is just awful in the summer. She has this lovely little condo with a lanai—that's what they call a screened-in porch down there—and she grows orchids on it. She actually sent me an orchid for my birthday last year, a purple one. I tried so hard to keep it alive. I read all the instructions, bought the special fertilizer, only gave it three ice cubes of water a week just like the tag said. But the leaves still turned yellow and it just completely died. I felt terrible about it. I just don't have a green thumb, I guess. My mother, though, she could grow anything. She had this huge vegetable garden when I was growing up... tomatoes, zucchini, cucumbers. We'd have fresh salads all summer long. But... oh, what was I saying? Right, feeling down for a few weeks. Honestly, I really can't say for sure if I've ever had a period like that before this whole six-month thing started. Nothing really stands out as being this bad for that long.
Before this current six-month period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for several weeks or more, even if it wasn't as long or as severe as this time?

Several weeks... you know, I'm really trying to rack my brain here, but no, I honestly don't think so. I mean, the only thing that lasts several weeks that completely drains my joy is our annual inventory at the shop. Oh, my goodness, talk about losing interest in things! By the second week of counting every single pair of socks and tiny little silver earring, you just want to pull your hair out. We use these little handheld scanners now, which are supposed to make it all so much easier, but half the time the battery dies or the barcode is smudged. 

Just last year, Sarah actually dropped one of the scanners right into a bucket of mop water. The night cleaning crew had left it out—which they are absolutely not supposed to do, I've told them a hundred times, it's a terrible slipping hazard. If a customer slipped, corporate would just have a field day with us. They are always looking for an excuse to cut our store hours anyway. They sent down this new regional manager last month, this young guy in a very shiny suit, who kept pacing around my floor talking about "synergy" and "foot traffic metrics." I just looked at him and thought, you wouldn't know how to sell a greeting card if your life depended on it. 

But... oh, I'm sorry, you were asking about feeling down. No, really, I can't remember ever feeling depressed or losing my joy for a few weeks before all this started. It really just seems to be this one long stretch lately.
Before this current six-month period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for a couple of weeks or more, even if it didn’t last as long as this time?

A couple of weeks... no, I really don't think so. I've been trying to think back, but honestly, nothing comes to mind. Well, actually, a couple of weeks is exactly how long my husband and I went to Italy for our 25th anniversary. Oh, it was just magnificent. We started in Rome, and the architecture... you just can't even imagine it until you're standing right there looking at the Colosseum. We had this tour guide, Lorenzo, who was just so passionate about the history. He waved his hands around the whole time he talked. 

We took the train up to Florence after that, and let me tell you, the gelato there is dangerous. I must have had a cone every single day. Stracciatella was my favorite—it's like chocolate chip, but the chocolate is in these fine little ribbons instead of chunks. I tried to find something similar at the grocery store when we got back, but that brand they sell in the plastic tubs just isn't the same. The lid on those tubs always cracks down the side anyway, and then the ice cream gets freezer burn. I ended up having to throw out a whole half-gallon of butter pecan last week because it tasted like ice crystals. My husband was so disappointed, butter pecan is his absolute favorite. He likes to put a little drizzle of caramel syrup on it... 

But anyway, no, to answer your question, I really haven't ever had a couple of weeks where I felt down or lost interest in things before this whole current thing started.

Before this current six-month period, have you ever had a time when you felt so down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks that it affected your daily life, like work, hobbies, or spending time with family?

At least two weeks... no, I really, honestly can't say that I have. I mean, my daily life is usually so busy, especially with the store. It's hard to even find two weeks to take off for a vacation, let alone let something affect my work for that long. Getting time off approved is like pulling teeth sometimes. You have to submit the request through this new online portal they rolled out in January, and it's just a nightmare to navigate. The font is so small, and if you click the wrong dropdown menu, it resets the whole form. 

My assistant manager, Brenda, she accidentally requested two weeks of unpaid leave instead of her vacation time, and it took payroll three whole pay cycles to fix it. Poor thing was so stressed out, she started stress-baking. She brought in these lemon bars that were just out of this world. She uses extra zest in the crust, which I never would have thought to do. I usually just stick to my grandmother's recipe for pound cake if I'm baking. It calls for a whole pound of butter, which sounds terrible for you, but it makes the cake so incredibly moist. I brought one to the neighborhood block party last summer, and Mrs. Higgins from three doors down asked for the recipe. She's the one with the two golden retrievers who are always digging up my hydrangeas... 

But, oh, right, affecting my daily life for two weeks. No, doctor, really, before these last six months, I've never had anything like that happen. This is really the first time it's been this bad.

Have you ever had a time in your life before this current six-month period when you felt so down, hopeless, or lost interest in things for at least two weeks in a row that it affected your daily life, even if it didn't last as long as this time?

Two weeks in a row of feeling hopeless... you know, I really don't think so. I mean, the only time I felt truly hopeless for two weeks straight was during our kitchen remodel a few years ago. Oh, what an absolute nightmare that was. We hired this contractor, Gary, who came highly recommended by my sister-in-law, but I swear the man operated in his own personal time zone. He told us it would be a quick job, and we ended up eating microwave dinners on folding trays in the living room for nearly three months. 

The dust was just... it was everywhere. You couldn't escape it. My dog, Buster, kept tracking these powdery white drywall footprints all over the oriental rug in the dining room. I finally had to go rent one of those heavy-duty carpet cleaners from the hardware store down the street, the ones that are so clunky you can barely lift them. And of course, the teenager working the rental counter didn't even offer to help me carry it out to the trunk. Kids these days just do not have the same customer service skills we were taught. I see it at my store all the time—they just want to lean against the cash wrap and look at their phones instead of folding the display tables. I have to constantly remind them that the floor needs to be completely fronted and faced before we lock the doors... 

Anyway, I'm sorry, I know I'm rambling again. But to answer your question, no. Before this current six-month spell, I've never had a time where I felt depressed or lost my interest in things for two weeks like that. This is the first time it's ever stuck around.
Before this current six-month period, have you ever had an episode where you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks in a row?

Two weeks in a row... no, I really can't say that I have. I mean, the only thing I can think of that lasted two weeks was that awful sinus infection I had back in 2018. Oh, it was just miserable. I went through three boxes of tissues, and not the cheap kind either, the ones with the lotion in them. If you use the regular ones, your nose gets so red and raw you look like Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer. 

I actually tried to find those lotion tissues at the pharmacy last week, but they completely rearranged the aisles. They moved all the cold and flu stuff over by the greeting cards, which makes absolutely no sense to me. Who wants to look at birthday cards when they're sneezing their head off? And the greeting card section is always so picked over anyway. I was trying to find a nice anniversary card for my niece, Sarah, and all they had left were those silly ones with the cartoon animals that play music when you open them. Sarah is turning 30 next month, she doesn't want a singing monkey on her card. She's a lawyer now, you know, works for a very prestigious firm downtown. They make her work ridiculous hours, though. She's always answering emails during Sunday dinner...

But, oh, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Right, feeling down for two weeks. No, doctor, before this current stretch, I really haven't ever experienced anything like that. This is definitely new for me.
Before this current six-month period, have you ever had an episode where you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks in a row?

Well, before this six-month period... no, I really don't think so. But this current stretch, it's just been so different. Most mornings lately I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling, you know? It's like the color has just drained out of everything before I even get dressed for the store. 

And getting dressed is a whole chore in itself these days. I have this closet full of clothes, but none of it feels right. I bought this beautiful plum-colored blazer from a boutique downtown—the one near the old cinema that closed last year—and I used to love wearing it. It has these really unique tortoiseshell buttons. But the dry cleaner on 4th Street, they chipped one of the buttons last time I took it in. I was so upset. I tried to find a replacement button online, but the shipping costs are just ridiculous. They charge more for shipping than the button itself! It's like how they get you with the printer ink. You buy a printer for practically nothing, and then you have to take out a second mortgage just to print a shipping label. My neighbor, Tom, he actually bought a laser printer because he got so fed up with the ink cartridges drying out. He prints all the flyers for the neighborhood watch meetings. We had a meeting last Tuesday because someone has been leaving their trash cans out on the curb for three days after pickup...

But I'm sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? Rambling. But yes, before these last six months, I never had a two-week period like that. It's just lately that I've been waking up with that awful gray feeling.

Before this current six-month period, have you ever had a time when you felt so down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks in a row that it affected your daily life, even if it didn’t last as long as this time?

I know you're trying to get a straight answer out of me, doctor, and I really am trying to think. But honestly, no. Before these last six months, I never had a two-week stretch where I felt down or lost interest in things. 

The only thing I can think of that lasted two whole weeks where I felt completely out of my element was when they sent me to that corporate training retreat in Chicago back in 2015. Oh, they had us stuck in this hotel near the airport, and the conference room was just freezing. They had the air conditioning cranked up so high you'd think they were storing meat in there. I had to wear my heavy winter coat indoors in July! And the food—they served us these sad little boxed lunches every single day. A turkey sandwich that was mostly dry bread, a tiny bag of chips, and an apple that looked like it had seen better days. 

I told our regional manager, Susan, that if they expected us to learn the new point-of-sale system, they needed to feed us proper meals. Susan is a sweet lady, but she gets so easily flustered. She was wearing this beautiful silk scarf during her presentation, and it just kept slipping off her shoulder every time she pointed at the projector. I actually saw a scarf just like it at a little shop downtown last weekend, but they wanted seventy dollars for it. Seventy dollars for a tiny square of fabric! I mean, you can get a whole outfit for that at my store if you know how to shop the clearance racks on a Tuesday. We do our markdowns on Monday nights, you see, so Tuesday morning is really the best time to come in before the good sizes get picked over...

But listen to me, I'm taking us off track again. I'm sorry. To answer your question for good, no. Before this current six-month spell, I never had any two-week periods where I felt depressed or hopeless. This is all completely new territory for me.
